article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Balanced to sativa-leaning hybrid
Genetics: OG Kush × S.A.G.E.
Breeder: T.H. Seeds
THC Content: 18–23%
CBD Content: Typically low
Terpene Profile: limonene , beta-caryophyllene , myrcene
Primary Flavors: Sage, sandalwood, earth, pine, herbs
Flowering Time (Indoor): 9–10 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: early to mid-October
Indoor Yield: 400–500 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: Moderate to high
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Kushage occupies an interesting place among old-school marijuana hybrids because it does not simply pile more heaviness onto the familiar Kush formula. T.H. Seeds deliberately paired OG Kush with S.A.G.E. to open the experience up, adding the latter plant’s brighter cerebral character and distinctive sandalwood-herbal flavor to the dense, powerful personality associated with OG genetics. The breeder lists the cultivar as a hybrid and gives it a 9–10 week flowering period, an indoor height of roughly 125–150 centimeters, and potential production around 400–500 grams per square meter.

That combination produces weed with an unmistakably classic character: pungent rather than candy-sweet, mentally active without abandoning its Kush foundation, and structured more elegantly than many compact OG descendants . Kushage also has historical credentials. T.H. Seeds’ catalog records a third-place finish in the seed-company category at the 2005 Cannabis Cup , giving the strain roots in an era before dessert and candy genetics came to dominate dispensary menus.
Genetics and Lineage

The official genetic formula is OG Kush × S.A.G.E. T.H. Seeds describes the OG Kush parent as providing the powerful Kush side of the cross, while S.A.G.E. was selected to supply the sativa influence needed to lift and sharpen that heavier character. Rather than producing a conventional sleepy Kush, the breeding goal was therefore balance: retain the depth, resin production, and intensity of OG while introducing more mental clarity, vertical growth, and aromatic complexity.

S.A.G.E., short for Sativa Afghani Genetic Equilibrium, has its own well-documented pedigree within the T.H. Seeds program. The breeder currently lists it as Big Sur Holy × Afghani , describes it as mostly sativa, and associates it with pine, sage, sandalwood, sweetness, and an uplifting creative effect. Those traits explain much of what distinguishes Kushage from more straightforward OG hybrids.

The result can show noticeable phenotype variation. Some plants lean closer to OG Kush, forming tighter flowers and emphasizing earth, fuel, and physical relaxation. Others reveal more S.A.G.E. influence through longer branches, stretched flower clusters, woody spice, and a livelier cerebral experience. That diversity is part of the cultivar’s appeal, but it also means THC percentages, terpene concentrations, aroma, and plant structure should never be treated as perfectly uniform.
Effects and Experience

Kushage tends to develop in stages rather than announcing itself with immediate sedation. The first portion of the experience is generally cerebral: attention feels sharpened, mood may rise, and ordinary thoughts can become more engaging. Creative work, music, conversation, gaming, or other activities that reward immersion may fit this phase particularly well. T.H. Seeds itself characterizes the effects as euphoric, happy, relaxed, tingly, and appetite stimulating.

As time passes, the OG Kush contribution becomes more evident. Physical tension may soften and the body can feel heavier without necessarily producing the complete couch-lock associated with very sedating indica-dominant marijuana. The contrast between an active headspace and progressively calmer body is the defining feature. For experienced consumers, that balance can make Kushage adaptable enough for late afternoon or evening use.

Potency deserves respect. Material testing near or above 20% THC can produce an intense experience for someone with limited tolerance, particularly when inhaled rapidly. Excessive THC may also contribute to temporary anxiety, dizziness, impaired attention, increased heart rate, or an uncomfortable sense of overstimulation. Starting conservatively remains more useful than relying on a strain name to predict exactly how a particular batch will feel.
Medical Benefits

From a medical marijuana perspective, Kushage is most logically considered a THC-dominant cultivar rather than a CBD-rich therapeutic strain. Its combination of mental elevation, physical relaxation, and appetite stimulation may explain why some patients choose similar cannabis products when dealing with persistent discomfort, reduced appetite, tension, or difficulty unwinding. Its relatively balanced subjective character may also appeal to patients who dislike marijuana that becomes immediately incapacitating.

Those potential applications should not be mistaken for Kushage-specific clinical evidence. Medical research generally evaluates cannabinoids, standardized preparations, or broader cannabis categories rather than named commercial strains. The National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health notes evidence of modest benefit from cannabis or cannabinoids for some forms of chronic pain, while evidence for many other conditions remains limited or uncertain.

Anyone using cannabis alongside prescription medication should also consider possible interactions and impairment. THC-dominant weed can affect coordination, judgment, and alertness, and individual responses differ significantly according to dose, tolerance, route of administration, and cannabinoid profile. A strain description can help characterize the cultivar, but it cannot substitute for individualized medical guidance.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

The aromatic identity of Kushage is where the S.A.G.E. heritage becomes especially obvious. Instead of leading with fruit or confectionery sweetness, dried flowers tend toward earth, crushed herbs, sage, woody spice, pine, and a distinctive sandalwood quality. T.H. Seeds specifically highlights earthy, herbal, sage, sandalwood, and spicy flavors, with the sandalwood component directly attributed to S.A.G.E.

Breaking apart a well-cured flower can uncover sharper layers beneath that woody foundation. Peppery spice and resinous pine may become more pronounced, while some phenotypes develop touches of citrus or Kush-like pungency. The likely terpene contributors include caryophyllene, pinene, myrcene, and limonene, although the actual terpene percentages can shift significantly between individual plants and harvests.

Smoke or vapor generally follows the aroma more closely than modern cannabis strains bred around extreme candy flavors. Herbal and woody notes dominate the opening, followed by spice and an earthy Kush finish. A proper cure is particularly valuable because overly rapid drying can flatten the subtle sage and sandalwood qualities that give this cultivar much of its personality.
Growing Information

Kushage grows with more reach than a compact OG Kush plant. T.H. Seeds places mature indoor height around 125–150 centimeters and describes the cross as producing larger yields and more elegantly formed plants than its OG parent. Flowering normally requires 9–10 weeks, with indoor production around 400–500 grams per square meter under successful conditions.

Branch development can be vigorous, particularly in S.A.G.E.-leaning individuals. Growers working with limited vertical room therefore need to account for stretch before flowering is well underway. An open canopy also helps light penetrate the numerous flowering sites created along the branches. Mature flowers can become substantial and resinous, making structural support useful once weight begins accumulating late in bloom.

Outdoors, the strain performs best where autumn remains warm and reasonably dry long enough for its extended flowering cycle to finish. October is the normal harvest window, with later-finishing phenotypes potentially requiring patience. Grow difficulty is best considered moderate: the genetics are vigorous, but controlling height, supporting developing branches, and protecting flowers from excessive late-season humidity require more attention than a compact, fast-finishing beginner cultivar.
FAQ
Is Kushage an indica or sativa?

T.H. Seeds officially classifies Kushage as a hybrid. Its S.A.G.E. parent introduces a significant sativa influence, so the experience and growth pattern can feel more energetic and elongated than those of many OG Kush crosses.
What are the genetics of Kushage?
The breeder-confirmed lineage is OG Kush × S.A.G.E. T.H. Seeds identifies S.A.G.E. itself as Big Sur Holy × Afghani and describes it as mostly sativa.
How strong is Kushage?

Kushage is generally encountered as THC-dominant marijuana, with commercial examples commonly falling around the high teens to low 20% range. Potency can vary considerably depending on phenotype, cultivation, harvest timing, and laboratory testing.
What does Kushage taste like?

Its signature flavor combines sage, sandalwood, earthy herbs, pine, and peppery spice. OG-leaning expressions may bring more pungent earthiness, while S.A.G.E.-dominant plants can emphasize woody incense and herbal notes.
How long does Kushage take to flower?
T.H. Seeds gives Kushage an indoor flowering period of 9–10 weeks. Outdoors, plants generally mature during October when grown in an appropriate climate.
Final Thoughts on Kushage

Kushage represents a period of cannabis breeding when Kush genetics were being deliberately crossed with more expansive sativa lines rather than simply reinforced with additional indica weight. OG Kush supplies potency, resin, earthy depth, and physical relaxation, while S.A.G.E. introduces sandalwood, herbs, longer growth, and a clearer cerebral direction. That contrast gives the finished marijuana a recognizable identity instead of reducing it to another variation on the OG theme.

Its moderate cultivation demands, respectable yield, distinctive old-school aroma, and layered effect have helped the cultivar remain relevant long after its 2005 Cannabis Cup recognition. For consumers interested in classic weed genetics—and growers who appreciate plants combining OG density with a more graceful sativa-influenced structure—Kushage remains one of the more distinctive hybrids preserved in the T.H. Seeds catalog.
